page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-480GB-2xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 24 physical cores and a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 480.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a combined 160 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data shows strong performance across memory and processing tasks. The server achieved a top-tier result in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.63 GB/sec and strong multi-threaded decompression at 355.23 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4086.55 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 290.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For LLM inference using a small 135M model, the system processed prompts at 10457.59 tokens/sec and generated text at 366.07 tokens/sec, placing it in the top tier.

While the hardware profile offers massive memory density and high-end GPU acceleration, there are notable architectural tradeoffs. The CPU allocation is designated as shared, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-tenant CPU loads. Additionally, the server lacks local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be handled externally. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of system memory relative to vCPUs and the inclusion of dual H100 GPUs make it a specialized, resource-dense option for workloads that prioritize GPU and memory capacity over dedicated CPU cores or local disk space.

This server is designed for workloads requiring substantial parallel processing and memory capacity. Suitable applications include large language model inference, data science tasks, high-throughput database operations, and memory-intensive computations.
